To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sequential fixed-width confidence interval procedures for the end points of a support of a non-regular distribution based on the extreme order statistics are proposed.

sequential estimation of the endpoints of the support of a non-regular distribution can be achieved by the use of a sequential procedure based on the range, and that such a procedure is asymptotically efficient.

the sequential procedures based on the range of order statistics are asymptotically efficient, and that the sequential fixed-width confidence interval based on the range is more efficient than the sequential fixed-width interval based on the maximum likelihood estimator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the sequential estimation of the support of a non-regular distribution.
sequential estimation of the extreme values of a non-regular distribution with bound support.
sequential point estimation in a non-regular case.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the results are not entirely satisfactory, the problem of estimation of the end-points of a support of a distribution is an important one, and deserves further study.

sequential estimation of the support end points based on the extreme observations is asymptotically efficient and the sequential fixed-width confidence interval procedures have the best possible asymptotic properties.
the sequential procedures based on the range have the best asymptotic properties among the procedures considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a sequential procedure for estimation of the end point of a support of the distribution based on the extreme order statistics.
the asymptotic properties of the estimators based on the range can be obtained in a similar way to the case of regular distributions.

, in the case where the underlying distribution has bounded support, we propose sequential fixed-width confidence procedures for the end points of support based on the range and show that they are asymptotically efficient, and we propose an asymptotically efficient sequential estimator of the support end point under squared loss plus sampling cost.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotic results for the sequential estimation of the support end points are similar to the results for the regular case.
the sequential procedures can be more efficient than their nonsequential counterparts.
the range based stopping rules are optimal in the sense that they minimize the asymptotic expected cost of the sequential procedure.
